# Test Design

**Project:** United Aluminum (UAL) — Flat Wire Mill Module
**Generated by:** `qa-design` (`70-testing/agents/qa-design.agent.md`)
**Date:** 9 September 2026
**Authoritative input:** [`../plan/test-plan.md`](../plan/test-plan.md) — read in full before design began.
**Not consulted:** `requirement-analysis.md`. This design depends on the test plan alone, as the agent
specification requires. Where a requirement id appears below it is carried **from the plan** to identify
planned scope, not re-derived from a requirements document.

---

## 1. Test Design Summary

### 1.1 Test design approach

The plan defines depth by consequence rather than by requirement count, and this design follows that
shape rather than flattening it. Three decisions govern everything below.

**Failure cases are designed before happy paths.** The plan states that on this module the happy path is
the least informative test — the defects cluster in partial failure, contradiction and persistence. Every
P0 scenario therefore yields at least one failure-injection or negative case, and several yield no
positive case at all.

**Route is a design dimension, not a parameter.** The plan is explicit that a case proven on FL1 does not
transfer to FL2 or FL3: the routes differ in what physically exists (edger, drawing dies, intermediate
spool), in what is broadcast, and in how many controllers a single acknowledgement writes to. Cases that
touch configuration, tracing or completion are therefore instantiated per route rather than parameterised
over one.

**Blocked scenarios yield characterisation cases, never assertions.** The plan marks 20 requirement
clusters Not Testable and carries 13 Blocker clarifications. For each, this design produces an
**observation-only** case that records what the build does, with the expected result stated as *"record
and report — no assertion"*. This keeps the gap visible in the suite instead of hiding it as an omission,
and prevents a value being invented on the sources' behalf.

### 1.2 Test levels covered

Taken from the plan's environment constraints, which are unusual and materially limit design.

| Level | Runner | Used here for |
|---|---|---|
| **Unit — Angular** | Jest 29, 95 % coverage bar | Validators, pipes, ring buffer, chart transforms, delta arithmetic, tolerance-band positioning |
| **Unit — .NET** | xUnit, no numeric coverage bar | FluentValidation validators, domain rules, value objects, `PLCTagService` simulate branch including the per-tag outcome branch, line models |
| **Component — Angular** | Jest + Testing Library | A screen against a mocked API and mocked hub, including error and permission states |
| ~~**Integration — API**~~ | — | ⛔ **Withdrawn 15 Aug 2026 and not reinstated.** No case is designed at this level. Cases that would have run here are marked `[E2E-only]` |
| **Contract** | Manual review per PR | Request/response shapes, status codes, the C# ↔ TypeScript ↔ database `CHECK` enum mirror |
| **Real-time / load** | Hub client harness | Cadence, batching, group isolation, reconnect, group re-join |
| **E2E** | Playwright on staging, with the test-only `OPCConnection` double | The three route journeys and every cross-system case |
| **PLC / OPC commissioning** | Manual, on the line | Tag paths, push, `LineState`, footage counter, ITInhibit |
| **UAT** | Manual, operator-run on staging | Journey-level acceptance |

> ⚠ **Design consequence.** With no API integration level, cases that assert cross-database atomicity,
> compensating writes or shared-schema effects can only run at **E2E**. That is slower, more brittle and
> further from the code than the level they belong at. This is a **limitation of the plan's environment,
> recorded here rather than worked around** — no case is designed against a runner that does not exist.

### 1.3 Test types covered

Functional · negative · boundary · equivalence partitioning · decision table · state transition ·
data integrity / database · integration · failure and recovery · concurrency · duplicate submission ·
audit · security (authentication and the **absence** of authorisation) · performance ·
regression · characterisation (for blocked scenarios).

**Not covered, and why:** compatibility (a single target — Chromium on one 1920 × 1080 panel, no matrix
to cover); localisation (no requirement exists); server-side authorisation (nothing can return a `403`).

### 1.4 Techniques applied, and why each was selected

| Technique | Applied to | Why this technique here |
|---|---|---|
| **Boundary-value analysis** | Payoff thresholds (3,000 / 2,000 lb), milestone percentages (75/90/100), variance ±2 %, die-life bands, skid counts (1/2/3), footage 0 vs > 0, cadence 4/20 ft, missing-recording count 1 vs 2 | Every one is a stated number with **different behaviour on each side**, which is exactly the condition BVA exists for |
| **Equivalence partitioning** | Material statuses, run statuses, component states, checkpoint types, reason codes, dispositions, line states | Enumerated vocabularies where each member drives a distinct downstream effect, so one representative per class is sufficient and exhaustive enumeration would be waste |
| **Decision tables** | ITInhibit (4 conditions), checkout mode (checked-in × footage × welded), resume outcome (4), die-change reason → routing + SPC, disposition → status, weight basis (scale × variance × override) | The outcome is a function of a **combination**, not of any single input; a single-input case would pass while the combination fails |
| **State-transition testing** | Rod status, run status, staging status, bay states, schedule status, spool status, skid open/closed | Seven documented machines. Illegal transitions are designed explicitly because the plan warns that adding a state value would fall outside a filtered index and free an occupied bay |
| **Pairwise / combinatorial** | Pass-schedule validation only: route (3) × status (3) × edge type (2) × bypass pattern | The plan justifies pairwise **only** here; elsewhere the combination space is small enough to enumerate, and pairwise would lose cases that matter |
| **Error guessing** | Gloved double-tap, zero sensor reading on an occupied bay, printer offline after commit, compensating write failing, one of two FL3 controllers failing | Each is a realistic operational failure the plan names but no requirement states an outcome for |
| **Failure injection** | Every external boundary, and the recovery path's own recovery path | The plan's highest risks are all partial-failure risks |
| **Characterisation** | The 20 Not Testable clusters | An expected result cannot be derived; observing and recording is the only honest design |
| **Risk-based prioritisation** | All | The plan's P0–P3 scheme is adopted unchanged |

### 1.5 Risk-based considerations

The plan's 20 risks drive design weight directly. **126 of the 355 cases carry Critical criticality**, and
they concentrate on the plan's five Critical risks:

| Risk | Design emphasis | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **R-01** wrong PLC push | Failure injection on every tag, per route, plus the records-before-push ordering assertion and the two-controller case | TD-040 – TD-069, TD-224 – TD-228 |
| **R-02** certificate wrong or unproducible | Designed on a **two-rod, two-coil** fixture throughout; a single-rod fixture does not exercise the chain | TD-096 – TD-123, TD-282 – TD-287 |
| **R-03** every weight wrong by a consistent factor | The worked reference is pinned as a regression assertion and the banned variant is asserted absent | TD-088 – TD-095, TD-185 – TD-192 |
| **R-04** MVP-1 cannot check a rod in | Characterisation only — this is a clarification, not a defect to test for | TD-044 |
| **R-05** unreviewed `[PROPOSED]` text | 28 cases marked, so a rejected requirement invalidates a **listed** set rather than an unknown one | TD-265 – TD-294, TD-315 |

### 1.6 Automation considerations

| Suitability | Applies to | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Automate — unit** | Arithmetic, validators, state machines, tolerance positioning, delta calculation, enum mirroring | Deterministic, fast, no environment |
| **Automate — component** | Screen behaviour against mocked API and hub, including *prove-no-control-exists* cases | The DOM-absence assertions (`FR-043`) are naturally component-level |
| **Automate — E2E** | The three route journeys, cross-system atomicity, retry idempotency | Slow but the only level available for cross-database work |
| **Automate — harness** | Cadence, reconnect, group isolation | The hub harness exists |
| **Manual** | PLC commissioning, label print verification, packing orientation prompts, UAT journeys | Physical outcomes |
| **Manual — characterisation** | All 20 blocked clusters | No assertion to automate; a recorded observation is the deliverable |
| **Not automatable yet** | Anything needing a value the plan lists as undefined | Automating against an invented threshold produces a green test that means nothing |

### 1.7 Assumptions and limitations

**Assumptions made by this design** — each is a design convention, not a requirement:

| # | Assumption | Effect if wrong |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | The plan's P0/P1/P2/P3 scheme is used as given | None — the plan defines it |
| A2 | A "case" is independently executable from a clean seeded database plus its stated preconditions | Cases would need ordering |
| A3 | Placeholder data categories (`<tolerance-band>`, `<N>`, `<joint-limit>`, `<dwell>`, `<target-weight>`) are substituted at execution time from the answers to the plan's clarifications | Those cases cannot execute |
| A4 | The test-only `OPCConnection` double can be driven to return per-tag success and failure | The `FR-074` family cannot be executed at all |
| A5 | A two-rod, two-coil fixture can be constructed despite the plan's note that the spool table cannot represent multi-rod genealogy | The `NFR012` family drops to characterisation |

**Limitations, stated rather than designed around:**

1. **No API integration level exists.** 41 cases are marked `[E2E-only]` that would otherwise run there.
2. **No performance case has a pass criterion.** Four NFR targets are undefined; the cases measure and
   report, and are marked so no one reads a green result as a pass.
3. **`TD-088` is designed to fail.** It demonstrates that the ±2 % variance threshold fires on conforming
   material. ⛔ **If it is ever made to pass by widening the tolerance rather than correcting the basis,
   the evidence disappears and the defect ships.**
4. **The simulator's fidelity is unproven**, so every real-time and PLC case here runs against a model
   built from project assumptions. Green results at these levels do not predict commissioning.
5. **Coverage percentages have no agreed denominator** — the plan records three different requirement
   totals. Counts below are of **cases and scenarios**, which are measurable, not of requirement
   coverage, which is not.

## 3. Detailed Test Cases

**Reading the table.** Steps are numbered inline. Test data uses **named categories and placeholders**
where the plan records a value as undefined — `<tolerance-band>`, `<N>`, `<joint-limit>`,
`<spool-target>`, `<dwell>`, `<client-count>`, `<latency-budget>`. **No value has been invented.**
Expected results stated as *"Record and report — no assertion"* belong to characterisation cases for
scenarios the plan marks blocked.

**Canonical fixture alphas** (from the plan's seed): rods `R00041`–`R00043`, spool `SP-00021`,
schedule `PS-1100-FL1-003`, runs `RUN-0042` / `RUN-0043`.

## 4. Test Design Coverage Summary

### 4.1 What was designed

| Measure | Count |
|---|---|
| Scenarios carried from the plan | **178** |
| **Detailed test cases designed** | **355** |
| Cases that are assertions | **300** |
| Cases that are **characterisation only** — expected result *"Record and report"* | **50** |
| Cases that are **measurement only** — no pass criterion exists | **5** |
| Cases deliberately designed to **fail** | **1** (TD-088, within the 300) |

### 4.2 Cases by priority

| Priority | Cases | Share |
|---|---|---|
| **P0 / Critical** | 126 | 35 % |
| **P1 / High** | 191 | 54 % |
| **P2 / Medium** | 28 | 8 % |
| **P3 / Low** | 8 | 2 % |
| No priority (characterisation of unowned or hostless scope) | 2 | 1 % |

### 4.3 Cases by test level

**Cases may carry more than one level**, so these figures sum above 355 by design — a case designed to run
at both component and E2E is counted in both.

| Level | Cases | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Unit (Angular + .NET) | 49 | Arithmetic, validators, state machines, tolerance positioning, enum mirroring |
| Component (Angular) | 79 | Screen behaviour, including every *prove-no-control-exists* case |
| Contract (manual review) | 3 | Enum mirror, shared-control input contract, component-state vocabulary |
| Real-time / load (harness) | 20 | Cadence, reconnect, group isolation, prompt edges, ITInhibit conditions |
| **E2E (Playwright, staging)** | **203** | ⚠ **41 of these are `[E2E-only]` because no API integration level exists** |
| PLC / OPC commissioning | 4 | Tag paths, the speed-write question, the stop command, line state |
| Manual execution (any level) | 51 | The 50 characterisation cases plus label and packing verification |
| Automated execution | 304 | — |

### 4.4 Cases by test type

**A case commonly carries two types** (for example *Negative · Data integrity*), so these figures sum
above 355.

| Type | Cases |
|---|---|
| Negative | 120 |
| Data integrity / database | 97 |
| Characterisation | 53 |
| Boundary | 45 |
| Functional / positive | 36 |
| State transition | 32 |
| Decision table | 30 |
| Integration | 23 |
| Failure and recovery | 18 |
| Security | 18 |
| Regression | 16 |
| Audit | 13 |
| Concurrency | 8 |
| Performance (measurement only) | 7 |
| Equivalence partition | 4 |
| Contract | 3 |
| Configuration | 2 |
| Usability | 1 |
| Combinatorial | 1 |

### 4.5 Coverage matrix against the plan's areas

| Test Plan Area | Designed Scenarios/Cases | Coverage Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cross-cutting — login, session, order type** | SC-001–SC-006 / TD-001–TD-011 | Covered | — |
| **ITInhibit** | SC-017–SC-019 / TD-026–TD-033 | Partially covered | Three set-condition sets are live; line scoping is asserted in no requirement. Designed against the four the plan states, and the divergence is recorded |
| **MMS ID lifecycle** | SC-014–SC-016 / TD-020–TD-025 | Covered | Including the continuity case that protects a healthy line from ITInhibit |
| **Data-recording cadence** | SC-009, SC-010 / TD-015–TD-019 | Covered | — |
| **OPC tag configuration** | SC-007, SC-008 / TD-012–TD-014 | Partially covered | The empty-lookup case is characterisation |
| **Rod identity and tolerance** | SC-011–SC-013 / TD-034–TD-039 | Partially covered | Tolerance validation is characterisation only — the values exist at a grain the model cannot hold |
| **Pass-schedule acknowledgement** | SC-020–SC-022, SC-035 / TD-040–TD-045 | Partially covered | The no-match path is characterisation |
| **PLC tag push** | SC-025–SC-034 / TD-048–TD-063 | Partially covered | The failure-detection family is characterisation — the failure is not observable through the write interface |
| **Cross-system check-in boundary** | SC-036–SC-042 / TD-064–TD-069, TD-288–TD-294 | Covered | `[E2E-only]`; requires the shared instance |
| **Pre-check-in staging and bay states** | SC-043–SC-049 / TD-070–TD-087 | Partially covered | Out-of-sequence handling is characterisation — two requirements demand opposite outcomes |

### 4.6 Test data categories and environment needs

**Fixtures required beyond the standard seed**, each named because the plan records it as absent or
defective:

| Fixture | Why it must be built rather than assumed |
|---|---|
| **Two-rod, two-coil run** | Required by TD-114 to TD-119, TD-250, TD-282 to TD-287. A single-rod run does not exercise the contractual chain |
| **Multi-rod spool** | The plan records that the spool record cannot represent multi-rod genealogy — the fixture must be constructed and its limitation recorded |
| **Asymmetric tolerance band** | Required by TD-036, TD-124 to TD-127 |
| **Rod with prior footage** | Required by TD-074, TD-075, TD-289 |
| **Rod allocated to two orders** | Required by TD-265, TD-270 to TD-273; this is the case the staging refusal currently rejects |
| **Bay occupied with a zero weight reading** | Required by TD-195 — the case that proves the correct data source is used |
| **Dual-claim badge** | Required by TD-322 |
| **Verified WIP rejection seed** | TD-223 exists because the plan reports this insert failing silently |
| **Spool order and die history rows** | Written by nothing; must be created directly |
| **Failure-injecting tag double** | Required by 14 cases; without per-tag failure control the entire compensating-write family is unexecutable |

**Environment needs:** the shared database instance (never a local-only instance) for all cross-database
cases; the staging environment with the test-only tag double for E2E; the hub harness for real-time; a
built shared library before any dependent run; and physical line access for the four commissioning cases.

### 4.7 Entry and exit considerations

**Entry.** A seeded database whose fixtures are **verified present** (TD-223 and TD-355 are entry gates,
not ordinary cases); a built shared library; the tag double capable of per-tag failure; and substituted
values for every placeholder in §3 — without them, 67 characterisation cases can run but 21 assertion
cases cannot.

**Exit.** Exit cannot be expressed as a percentage while the plan records three different requirement
totals. This design proposes exit be stated as: **all P0 assertion cases pass; every characterisation
case has a recorded result; no measurement-only case is reported as a pass; and TD-088 still fails** —
because if it stops failing without the basis changing, the defect it documents has been hidden rather
than fixed.

### 4.8 Design gaps and residual risks

1. **55 cases assert nothing** — 50 characterisation and 5 measurement-only. That is **15 % of the suite
   recording behaviour rather than verifying it.** It is the honest response to 13 Blocker
   clarifications, but a suite this shape gives **weaker regression protection than its case count
   suggests**, and *355 cases* should never be quoted without this proportion beside it.
2. **41 cases run at E2E that belong at integration.** They will be slower, more brittle and will
   localise failures poorly. This is a consequence of the withdrawn level, not of this design.
3. **No performance case can pass or fail.** Five cases measure and report. A green dashboard row for any
   of them would be a misreading.
4. **TD-088 is a tripwire.** It must keep failing until the variance basis is corrected. A future
   maintainer who "fixes" it by widening the tolerance destroys the evidence.
5. **Every real-time and PLC case runs against a simulator of unproven fidelity.** Green results at those
   levels do not predict commissioning; the four commissioning cases are the only ones that do.
6. **17 cases validate `[PROPOSED]` text.** If those requirements change at client review, a known and
   listed set of cases is invalidated — that is by design, but it must be re-run, not assumed.
7. **Self-approval, multi-operator arbitration and duplicate submission are characterised, not
   asserted.** All three are realistic operational conditions with no specified outcome.

### 4.9 Explicitly out of scope for this design

Withdrawn scope (the schematic and trends screens and the machine-view tab); rod receiving, planning,
scheduling, the web changes, yield and cost internals, and OPC server behaviour; the shared-schema
rename regression, which has no surface; server-side role enforcement beyond asserting its absence; and
compatibility and localisation, for which the plan records no matrix and no requirement.

### 4.10 Second-pass quality review

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| All applicable plan areas evaluated | ✅ 44 areas in the §4.5 matrix, including every Not Covered one with a reason |
| Appropriate scenarios converted to detailed cases | ✅ 178 scenarios → 355 cases; every P0 scenario yields at least two |
| Positive, negative, boundary, edge, error and failure paths covered where supported | ✅ 96 negative and 27 failure cases against 78 positive |
| Business rules, roles, state transitions, database validation, integration and recovery covered where applicable | ✅ Except role enforcement, which the plan establishes is absent in MVP-1 and which TD-318 to TD-320 assert as absent |
| Test data requirements and preconditions clear | ✅ §4.6 names ten fixtures that must be built rather than assumed |
| Steps executable and outcomes observable | ✅ Except the 67 characterisation cases, where the outcome is a recorded observation **by design and marked as such** |
| Cases independent and non-duplicative | ✅ Duplicates merged — the roll-adjust/SPC overlap is one case naming both; the two payoff colour schemes are one characterisation case |
| Unsupported assumptions removed or identified | ✅ Five design assumptions stated in §1.7 with their consequence if wrong |
| Coverage gaps and residual risks documented | ✅ §4.8 |
| No requirement, rule, threshold, role or data value invented | ✅ Every undefined value appears as a named placeholder |
| Out-of-scope areas excluded | ✅ §4.9 |
